column1: What does 'thin-film deposition' refer to in chip manufacturing?
column2: The discipline of growing controlled films of material — insulators, metals, semiconductors — onto the wafer surface with precise thickness and composition.

column1: To what approximate pressure does a deposition chamber evacuate?
column2: ~10⁻⁶ torr — about a billionth of atmospheric pressure.

column1: What does the wafer sit on inside a deposition chamber?
column2: A heated chuck, often called a susceptor.

column1: In PVD, what mechanism knocks atoms off the target?
column2: Argon ions from a plasma slam into the solid target (the sputtering target), knocking atoms loose.
Atoms travel in straight lines from target to wafer; they cannot coat the bottoms of high-aspect-ratio trenches.

column1: What precursor gas does CVD use to deposit silicon?
What makes CVD conformal where PVD is not?
column2: CVD deposition is mediated by gas-phase chemistry, so precursors flow into recesses equally well on horizontal and vertical surfaces.
Pulse precursor A (surface saturates), purge, pulse precursor B (reacts to form one monolayer), purge — repeat.

column1: What film is grown by ALD using hafnium and water-vapor precursors?
column2: HfO₂ — hafnium oxide, used as a high-k gate dielectric.

column1: Why is ALD slow, and roughly how long does a single high-quality ALD film take?
column2: Because it deposits exactly one atomic layer per cycle; a single high-quality film can take an hour.
